scope: Local CPU regression checks for timing and single/batched saliency precision
confirmed_regression: A real float64 convolutional model passed to compute_explanation with Saliency returned None after RuntimeError: Input type (float) and bias type (double) should be the same. Both the repository's numpy.float32 conversion and Quantus's torch.Tensor numpy conversion forced float32.
coverage: CLI default float32 and explicit float64 reach model loading, actual HybridDecomposer execution, actual Quantus/Captum Saliency and saved timing metadata
Synthetic model constructors replace pretrained torchvision downloads, one actual split iteration per model slot replaces twenty, and one synthetic image replaces the ImageNet-S validation set
Both precision paths produce finite saliency and finite nonnegative timing CSV values
Batched Saliency runs on two synthetic images in each precision and returns finite nonzero maps in the requested dtype
Custom ImageNet and ImageNet-S paths are forwarded and recorded
Timing config default resolves to an existing repository directory
Unsupported dtype is rejected before dataset loading
Absolute CLI script invocation with --help succeeds from /tmp
limitations: No pretrained models or datasets were downloaded; these checks do not reproduce the historical ImageNet timing benchmark
Only CPU execution and the Saliency attribution method were exercised
Other agents' optional sparse import repairs were present for the decomposition checks
The installed CUDA runtime reported an old-driver warning; execution was explicitly constrained to CPU
NumPy 2.4.4 in this narrow check does not establish compatibility with other Quantus metrics; the broader validation environment is recorded separately
review: Independent read-only code review found no blocking defect in the dtype/data-path propagation, portable root, metadata or tensor-preserving saliency calls.
